# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer

  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`

  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true

  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ci-sign — host-level signing mediator for self-hosted macOS runners.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS (gh-1865 / gh-1866, owner decision 2026-10-28)
#
# The fa-m5 pool is ONE Mac under ONE user account hosting several runner
# registrations (fa-m5-1/2/3, plus the yoloit / learn.ai / yoclip runners).
# Every signing job used to create its OWN temporary keychain and publish it
# through the PER-USER GLOBAL keychain search list. Two failure classes came
# out of that:
#
#   1. Eviction (gh-1866, runs 40165497544 → 40165498619): a fixed-list
#      writer replaced the whole search list and evicted a concurrent job's
#      keychain → "No certificate for team ... found".
#   2. Ambiguity (gh-1865, run 40455401630): the additive union helper fixed
#      (1) but left TWO same-subject certificates ("Apple Distribution:
#      Uladzimir Klyshevich (YP9HC3USZ3)", different serials — the iOS and
#      the macOS distribution certs) in one list; xcodebuild resolved the
#      generic name to the WRONG cert and the iOS archive died after ~24 min
#      ("Provisioning profile doesn't include signing certificate").
#   3. Interactive GUI keychain-password prompts on the owner's desktop:
#      runners live in the user's Aqua launchd session, and a leftover or
#      locked per-job keychain (empty password) makes SecurityAgent pop a
#      dialog mid-CI.
#
# THE MODEL: ONE persistent per-host keychain (ci-signing.keychain-db),
# provisioned ONCE and idempotently re-verified, holding every distribution
# identity. Signing jobs NEVER create or delete keychains and NEVER write
# the search list for signing purposes. Identity resolution is pinned by
# SHA-1 everywhere (xcodebuild CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY / codesign -s SHA1
# --keychain), so same-named certificates can coexist and legs stay
# parallel. `doctor` fail-fasts on profile/identity mismatches in seconds
# instead of after a dead archive.
#
# USAGE
#   ci-sign install <label>            import/refresh identity from env
#       reads CI_SIGN_<LABEL>_P12_B64 + CI_SIGN_<LABEL>_P12_PASSWORD, or
#       CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV / CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV naming the env vars
#       that hold them (legacy workflow secret names). Idempotent: a
#       re-run with the SAME certificate is a no-op; a DIFFERENT cert
#       replaces the previous one for the label. --force re-imports even
#       if the fingerprint matches.
#   ci-sign sha1 <label>               print the pinned SHA-1 fingerprint
#   ci-sign serial <label>             print the certificate serial (hex)
#   ci-sign name <label>               print the certificate common name
#   ci-sign codesign <label> [args…]   exec codesign --keychain <kc> -s <SHA1> args…
#   ci-sign doctor <profile>[ <label>] fail fast: every cert embedded in the
#                                      provisioning profile must match an
#                                      identity in the signing keychain
#   ci-sign unlock                     unlock the keychain non-interactively
#   ci-sign list                       list valid codesigning identities
#   ci-sign cleanup-legacy             best-effort delete known per-job
#                                      keychains left by older workflows
#   ci-sign path                       print the keychain path
#
# EXIT CODES: 0 ok; 1 operational failure (mismatch, missing identity);
# 2 usage error. When GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, failures emit ::error lines.
set -euo pipefail

# The keychain path is overridable for tests (CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN) — the
# default is the persistent host keychain. CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD
# already overrides the stored password the same way.
KC="${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN:-$HOME/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db}"
CFG="$HOME/.config/ci-sign"
KCPASS_FILE="$CFG/keychain-password"
LABELS_DIR="$CFG/labels"

err() { if [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ]; then echo "::error::ci-sign: $*"; else echo "ci-sign: $*" >&2; fi; }
die() { err "$*"; exit 1; }
usage() { echo "usage: ci-sign <install|sha1|serial|name|codesign|doctor|unlock|list|cleanup-legacy|path> ..." >&2; exit 2; }

[ $# -ge 1 ] || usage
CMD="$1"; shift

kc_password() {
  # Keychain password: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] if provided, else a stored
  # random one (created on first use). 0600 user-only file — it protects a
  # CI-only keychain whose certificates are already provisioned from repo
  # secrets by a trusted workflow.
  if [ -n "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ ! -s "$KCPASS_FILE" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    umask 077
    openssl rand -base64 32 > "$KCPASS_FILE"
  fi
  cat "$KCPASS_FILE"
}

ensure_keychain() {
  local kcpass
  kcpass="$(kc_password)"
  if [ ! -f "$KC" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    security create-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
  fi
  # No inactivity auto-lock; explicit unlock per operation keeps it honest.
  security set-keychain-settings -u "$KC" 2>/dev/null || true
  # Idempotent, additive, self-verifying search-list membership (gh-1866
  # logic, applied ONCE for a persistent entry — never per job). Skipped
  # for test keychains (CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN override) — they never leave the
  # test sandbox.
  if [ -z "${CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN:-}" ] && ! security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -qxF "$KC"; then
    local want current
    want="$KC $HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
    current="$(security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -v '^$' | grep -vxF "$KC" | tr '\n' ' ')"
    security list-keychains -d user -s $current "$KC"
    security list-keychains | sed 's/[[:space:]]//g; s/"//g' | grep -qxF "$KC" || die "failed to add keychain to search list"
  fi
  security unlock-keychain -p "$kcpass" "$KC"
}

do_unlock() {
  [ -f "$KC" ] || die "no signing keychain at $KC — run 'ci-sign install <label>' first (host provisioning)"
  security unlock-keychain -p "$(kc_password)" "$KC"
}

p12_env_value() { # p12_env_value <VARNAME>
  local var="$1"
  [ -n "${!var:-}" ] || die "env $var is not set"
  printf '%s' "${!var}"
}

label_env() { # label_env <label> <SUFFIX> -> prints resolved env var VALUE
  local label="$1" suffix="$2"
  local upper="${label^^}"
  upper="${upper//-/_}"
  if [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV:-}" ] || [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV:-}" ]; then
    # Legacy secret names, mapped explicitly by the caller.
    case "$suffix" in
      P12_B64)      [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV:-}" ]      && p12_env_value "$CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV"      && return 0 ;;
      P12_PASSWORD) [ -n "${CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV:-}" ] && p12_env_value "$CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV" && return 0 ;;
    esac
  fi
  p12_env_value "CI_SIGN_${upper}_${suffix}"
}

import_fingerprint() { # import_fingerprint <p12file> <password>; prints SHA1 (no colons)
  local tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064
  trap "rm -rf '$tmp'" RETURN
  openssl pkcs12 -passin "pass:$2" -in "$1" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$tmp/c.pem" 2>/dev/null \
    || openssl pkcs12 -passin "pass:" -in "$1" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$tmp/c.pem" 2>/dev/null \
    || return 1
  openssl x509 -in "$tmp/c.pem" -noout -fingerprint -sha1 2>/dev/null \
    | sed 's/^.*=//; s/://g'
}

verify_label_identity() { # verify_label_identity <label>; echoes sha1
  local label="$1"
  local mf="$LABELS_DIR/$label"
  local sha1
  [ -f "$mf" ] || die "label '$label' is not provisioned (no $mf) — run 'ci-sign install $label' first (host provisioning)"
  sha1="$(sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$mf")"
  [ -n "$sha1" ] || die "corrupt manifest for '$label'"
  do_unlock
  if ! security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC" | grep -qi "$sha1"; then
    die "identity $sha1 (label '$label') is not a VALID codesigning identity in the signing keychain — re-run 'ci-sign install $label --force'"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$sha1"
}

case "$CMD" in
  path)
    echo "$KC"
    ;;

  unlock)
    do_unlock
    echo "unlocked $KC"
    ;;

  list)
    do_unlock
    security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC"
    ;;

  install)
    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    FORCE=0; [ "${2:-}" = "--force" ] && FORCE=1
    # Concurrent installs (two matrix legs re-verifying on the same host)
    # serialize on a lock dir — create-keychain/import are not idempotent
    # under race; the happy path after first provisioning is a no-op that
    # holds the lock for milliseconds.
    LOCK="$CFG/install.lock"
    mkdir -p "$CFG"
    ACQUIRED=0
    for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
      if mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then ACQUIRED=1; break; fi
      sleep 2
    done
    [ "$ACQUIRED" -eq 1 ] || die "another ci-sign install holds the lock ($LOCK)"
    trap 'rmdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
    P12_B64="$(label_env "$LABEL" P12_B64)"
    P12_PW="$(label_env "$LABEL" P12_PASSWORD)"
    [ -n "$P12_B64" ] || die "empty P12 payload for label '$LABEL'"

    ensure_keychain
    TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
    # One consolidated EXIT trap (a second `trap ... EXIT` would REPLACE
    # the lock-release trap above, leaking the lock dir).
    trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"; rmdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
    printf '%s' "$P12_B64" | base64 --decode > "$TMP/cert.p12" 2>/dev/null || die "P12 payload for '$LABEL' is not valid base64"

    NEW_FP="$(import_fingerprint "$TMP/cert.p12" "$P12_PW")" || die "cannot read P12 for '$LABEL' (wrong password or corrupt payload?)"
    [ -n "$NEW_FP" ] || die "cannot read P12 for '$LABEL' (wrong password or corrupt payload?)"

    OLD_FP="$( [ -f "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL" ] && sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL" || true )"
    if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && [ "$NEW_FP" = "$OLD_FP" ]; then
      # Same certificate as the manifest claims — make sure it is REALLY a
      # valid identity (covers partial imports), then we are done.
      if security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC" | grep -qi "$NEW_FP"; then
        echo "ci-sign: identity for '$LABEL' is up to date ($NEW_FP)"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "ci-sign: manifest matches but identity invalid — re-importing"
    fi

    if [ -n "$OLD_FP" ] && [ "$OLD_FP" != "$NEW_FP" ]; then
      security delete-identity -Z "$OLD_FP" "$KC" 2>/dev/null \
        || err "could not remove previous identity $OLD_FP for '$LABEL' (continuing; stale identity remains)"
    fi

    security import "$TMP/cert.p12" -k "$KC" -P "$P12_PW" -T /usr/bin/codesign
    # Partition the private key so codesign never needs interactive auth
    # (this is what prevents GUI keychain prompts).
    security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$(kc_password)" "$KC" >/dev/null

    if ! security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KC" | grep -qi "$NEW_FP"; then
      die "imported P12 for '$LABEL' but it is not a valid codesigning identity (expired, revoked, or key/cert mismatch). Try 'ci-sign install $LABEL --force', then check the certificate in Apple Developer Portal."
    fi

    mkdir -p "$LABELS_DIR"
    CERT_PEM="$TMP/c.pem"
    openssl pkcs12 -passin "pass:$P12_PW" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$CERT_PEM" 2>/dev/null \
      || openssl pkcs12 -passin "pass:" -in "$TMP/cert.p12" -clcerts -nokeys -out "$CERT_PEM" 2>/dev/null || true
    SERIAL="$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT_PEM" -noout -serial | sed 's/^serial=//')"
    NAME="$(openssl x509 -in "$CERT_PEM" -noout -subject -nameopt multiline 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*commonName[^:]*://p' | head -1)"
    umask 077
    { echo "sha1=$NEW_FP"; echo "serial=$SERIAL"; echo "name=$NAME"; echo "updated=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"; } > "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL"

    echo "ci-sign: installed identity for '$LABEL': $NAME"
    echo "  sha1=$NEW_FP serial=$SERIAL"

    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    MF="$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL"
    case "$CMD" in
      sha1)   verify_label_identity "$LABEL"; echo ;;
      serial) sed -n 's/^serial=//p' "$MF" ;;
      name)   sed -n 's/^name=//p' "$MF" ;;
    esac
    ;;

  codesign)
    LABEL="${1:-}"; [ -n "$LABEL" ] || usage
    shift
    SHA1="$(verify_label_identity "$LABEL")"
    exec codesign --keychain "$KC" -s "$SHA1" "$@"
    ;;

    # Decode a provisioning profile to a plist on stdout WITHOUT touching
    # keychain state: `security cms -D` requires a default keychain (none
    # exists on this host by design — default-keychain writes are part of
    # the old race), openssl cms does not.
    PROFILE="${1:-}"
    [ -n "$PROFILE" ] && [ -f "$PROFILE" ] || die "profile not found: ${PROFILE:-<none>}"
    openssl cms -inform DER -verify -noverify -in "$PROFILE" -out /dev/stdout 2>/dev/null
    ;;

  doctor)
    PROFILE="${1:-}"; LABEL="${2:-}"
    [ -n "$PROFILE" ] || usage
    [ -f "$PROFILE" ] || die "profile not found: $PROFILE"
    do_unlock

    # The extraction must fail CLEAN on garbage input (a traceback here is
    # exactly the "guard error" obscurity the precheck exists to avoid).
    PROFILE_SERIALS="$(python3 - "$PROFILE" <<'PYEOF'
import plistlib, subprocess, sys
try:
    raw = subprocess.run(["openssl", "cms", "-inform", "DER", "-verify", "-noverify",
                          "-in", sys.argv[1], "-out", "/dev/stdout"],
                         capture_output=True)
    d = plistlib.loads(raw.stdout)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(3)
for c in d.get("DeveloperCertificates", []):
    r = subprocess.run(["openssl", "x509", "-inform", "DER", "-noout", "-serial"],
                       input=c, capture_output=True)
    s = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    if s.startswith("serial="):
        print(s[len("serial="):])
PYEOF
)" || true
    [ -n "$PROFILE_SERIALS" ] || die "could not extract certificates from profile $PROFILE (not a valid mobileprovision?)"

    KC_SERIALS="$(security find-certificate -a -p "$KC" 2>/dev/null | python3 -c '
import sys, re, subprocess
pem = sys.stdin.read()
for m in re.finditer(r"[REDACTED:PEM CERTIFICATE]", pem, re.S):
    r = subprocess.run(["openssl", "x509", "-noout", "-serial"], input=m.group(0).encode(), capture_output=True)
    s = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    if s.startswith("serial="):
        print(s[len("serial="):])
')"
    [ -n "$KC_SERIALS" ] || die "signing keychain has no readable identities — run 'ci-sign install <label>'"

    MISSING=0
    while IFS= read -r s; do
      [ -n "$s" ] || continue
      if ! printf '%s\n' "$KC_SERIALS" | grep -qxF "$s"; then
        err "profile $(basename "$PROFILE") embeds certificate serial $s which is NOT in the signing keychain — re-issue the profile under the current distribution certificate or run 'ci-sign install'"
        MISSING=1
      fi
    done <<EOF
$PROFILE_SERIALS
EOF
    [ "$MISSING" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

    if [ -n "$LABEL" ]; then
      WANT="$(sed -n 's/^serial=//p' "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "$WANT" ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$PROFILE_SERIALS" | grep -qxF "$WANT"; then
        err "profile $(basename "$PROFILE") does not contain the '$LABEL' identity (serial $WANT) — wrong profile secret for this certificate?"
        exit 1
      fi
    fi
    echo "ci-sign: doctor OK — $(basename "$PROFILE") certificates all present in signing keychain"
    ;;

  cleanup-legacy)
    # Best-effort removal of per-job keychains created by pre-ci-sign
    # workflows (they cause locked-keychain GUI prompts when orphaned).
    for name in build.keychain build-arm64.keychain build-x86_64.keychain build-macos.keychain; do
      security delete-keychain "$name" 2>/dev/null && echo "ci-sign: removed legacy keychain $name" || true
    done
    find "$HOME/Library/Keychains" -maxdepth 1 -name 'build*.keychain-db' -delete 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "ci-sign: legacy keychain cleanup done"
    ;;

  *)
    usage
    ;;
esac

# gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28) — host signing
# provisioning. Installs/refreshes the PERSISTENT host keychain
# (~/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db) with every distribution
# identity the repo's signing legs need, and sweeps the per-job keychains
# left behind by the retired workflows (their orphans produced interactive
# SecurityAgent keychain-password prompts in the owner's GUI session).
#
# Dispatch-only by design: this touches persistent host state, never a
# push/schedule. Idempotent — re-running with the SAME certificates is a
# no-op; after a certificate rotation re-run installs the new serial and
# retires the old identity for the label.
#
# First run performs the actual provisioning; every signing workflow also
# re-verifies its label via `ci-sign install <label>` (a no-op when
# up-to-date), so a drift between host and repo self-heals on the next
# signing run.
name: Host signing provision (ci-sign)

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  provision:
    name: Provision ci-sign host keychain
    # The keychain is HOST-global state (~/Library/Keychains/), and the
    # fa-m5 pool is three registrations on ONE host under ONE user — the
    # macos-m5 pool is correct routing (gh-1906: no workflow pins fa-m5-*
    # runner-NAME labels; a name label would silently match zero runners
    # and queue forever). Concurrent provisioning across registrations is
    # safe: ci-sign install is idempotent and serializes on its lock dir.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@8e8c483db84b4bed9817f72c0f3cd5f5aef4e7ee # v6.0.0

      - name: Install ci-sign onto the host PATH
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          cp scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          chmod +x "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          "$HOME/bin/ci-sign" path

      - name: Provision iOS distribution identity
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: IOS_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: IOS_P12_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${IOS_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::IOS_P12_BASE64 not set — iOS label not provisioned"
            exit 0
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install ios
          echo "ios sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 ios) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial ios) name=$(~/bin/ci-sign name ios)"

      - name: Provision macOS distribution identity
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 not set — macOS label not provisioned"
            exit 0
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install macos
          echo "macos sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 macos) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial macos) name=$(~/bin/ci-sign name macos)"

      - name: Provision macOS installer identity
        env:
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 not set — macos-installer label not provisioned (TestFlight PKG leg skips itself)"
            exit 0
          fi
          ~/bin/ci-sign install macos-installer
          echo "macos-installer sha1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 macos-installer) serial=$(~/bin/ci-sign serial macos-installer)"

      - name: Sweep legacy per-job keychains
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ~/bin/ci-sign cleanup-legacy
          echo "--- final state ---"
          ~/bin/ci-sign list

desc "Build iOS IPA only (for CI split build/submit pattern)"
  lane :build_only do
    # gh-1865 model v3: the signing identity lives in the PERSISTENT host
    # keychain (ci-signing.keychain-db), provisioned by the workflow via
    # ~/bin/ci-sign. No per-job keychain, no search-list writes here (the
    # additive-helper dance retired with per-job keychains — gh-1866/
    # gh-1865). Point-of-use unlock right before the archive: hours can
    # pass between the workflow's provision step and gym, and an explicit
    # unlock is immune to any gap length (the gh-1798 auto-lock window
    # hack is retired). gh-1910 lesson kept: resolve the script absolutely
    # from the Fastfile location (__dir__ = flutter_app/fastlane →
    # repo/scripts) — fastlane's sh does not honor the assumed lane cwd.
    ci_sign = File.expand_path("../../scripts/ci-sign", __dir__)
    sh(ci_sign, "unlock")

    team_id = ENV["IOS_TEAM_ID"] || "YP9HC3USZ3"
    bundle_id = ENV["IOS_BUNDLE_ID"] || "dev.fa1.app"
    profile_name = ENV["IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME"] || "Fa Profile"
    live_activity_profile_name = ENV["IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_NAME"] || "FaLiveActivity Profile"
    # gh-1865: CI passes a SHA-1 fingerprint (IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY read
    # from the job's own keychain right after import) — never resolve the
    # identity by NAME, which is a lottery when the additive per-user
    # search list holds two same-CN "Apple Distribution" certs from
    # concurrent signing legs. The bare name below is a LOCAL-dev fallback
    # only; the workflow always pins.
    signing_identity = ENV["IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY"] || "iPhone Distribution"

    update_code_signing_settings(
      use_automatic_signing: false,
      path: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj",
      team_id: team_id,
      bundle_identifier: bundle_id,
      profile_name: profile_name,
      code_sign_identity: signing_identity,
      # ONLY the app target: without this filter the action rewrites EVERY
      # target's PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER (incl. the FaLiveActivity
      # extension), producing a CFBundleIdentifier collision at upload.
      targets: ["Runner"]
    )

    # The FaLiveActivity extension signs MANUALLY as well: the runner's Xcode
    # has no Apple account, so automatic signing / -allowProvisioningUpdates
    # cannot create its profile — it is installed from a secret by the
    # workflow and only gets pointed at here.
    update_code_signing_settings(
      use_automatic_signing: false,
      path: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj",
      team_id: team_id,
      bundle_identifier: "#{bundle_id}.FaLiveActivity",
      profile_name: live_activity_profile_name,
      code_sign_identity: signing_identity,
      targets: ["FaLiveActivity"]
    )

    sh("flutter", "clean")
    sh("flutter", "pub", "get")
    cocoapods(podfile: "ios/Podfile")

    if ENV["BUILD_NUMBER"]
      increment_build_number(xcodeproj: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj", build_number: ENV["BUILD_NUMBER"])
    else
      increment_build_number(xcodeproj: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj")
    end

    # Issue #726 (run 35564638018): ASC closes a version train once a build
    # of it was approved (90186) and rejects submissions not higher than the
    # previously approved version (90062) — with pubspec pinned at 1.0.0 the
    # daily TestFlight upload can never land again. BUILD_NAME comes from
    # build-mobile.yml (the derived next-tag version, strictly increasing);
    # unset = legacy manual flow, keep the pubspec version.
    build_name_args = ENV["BUILD_NAME"] ? ["--build-name", ENV["BUILD_NAME"]] : []
    sh("xcrun simctl list > /dev/null 2>&1 || true")
    sh("xcrun simctl boot 'iPhone 16' 2>/dev/null || xcrun simctl boot 'iPhone 15' 2>/dev/null || true")
    sh("flutter", "build", "ios", "--release", "--no-codesign", *build_name_args)

    # gh-1692: xcbeautify, never xcpretty (xcpretty swallowed the archive
    # error — silent `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`), and on failure the newest
    # gym log tail lands in the job log via print_gym_log_tail.
    begin
      build_app(
        workspace: "ios/Runner.xcworkspace",
        scheme: "Runner",
        export_method: "app-store",
        output_directory: "build/ios/ipa",
        output_name: "fa.ipa",
        skip_build_archive: false,
        clean: true,
        sdk: "iphoneos",
        xcodebuild_formatter: "xcbeautify",
        export_options: {
          method: "app-store",
          provisioningProfiles: {
            bundle_id => profile_name,
            "#{bundle_id}.FaLiveActivity" => live_activity_profile_name
          },
          signingStyle: "manual",
          # gh-1865: pin the export step by the same fingerprint — the
          # exportOptions signingCertificate accepts a SHA-1 (that is what
          # Xcode itself writes into exportOptions plists), so
          # -exportArchive cannot resolve a shadowing same-CN cert either.

# frozen_string_literal: true

# gh-1910 — the build_only lane must invoke scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh
# via a path resolved from the Fastfile location (__dir__), not a relative
# ../scripts path that depends on the process cwd. On the runner fastlane's
# sh did not honor the assumed lane cwd, so the relative call failed with
# exit 127 (run 4032679374, Fastfile:453).
# Plain ruby, no gems:
#
#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/build_only_keychain_helper_test.rb
#
# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
# never executes the checks.

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  fastfile = File.expand_path("../Fastfile", __dir__)
  source = File.read(fastfile)

  # Extract the build_only lane body (up to the next `lane` or top-level
  # `end` at the same indent).
  lane_match = source.match(/^  lane :build_only do\n(.*?)^  end$/m)
  raise "FAIL: could not locate lane :build_only in Fastfile" unless lane_match

  lane_body = lane_match[1]

  raise "FAIL: build_only still calls the helper via relative ../scripts path (cwd-dependent)" \
    if lane_body.include?('sh("bash", "../scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh"')

  helper_expr = 'File.expand_path("../../scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh", __dir__)'
  raise "FAIL: build_only does not resolve the helper from the Fastfile location (#{helper_expr})" \
    unless lane_body.include?(helper_expr)

  # Both keychain branches (build.keychain-db and login.keychain-db) must use
  # the resolved helper, and the resolved file must actually exist. Resolve
  # from the Fastfile's directory (flutter_app/fastlane), not this test's.
  fastfile_dir = File.expand_path("..", __dir__)
  resolved = File.expand_path("../../scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh", fastfile_dir)
  raise "FAIL: resolved helper #{resolved} does not exist" unless File.exist?(resolved)

  raise "FAIL: build.keychain-db branch does not use the resolved helper" \
    unless lane_body.include?('sh("bash", keychain_helper, "#{Dir.home}/Library/Keychains/build.keychain-db")')
  raise "FAIL: login.keychain-db branch does not use the resolved helper" \
    unless lane_body.include?('sh("bash", keychain_helper, "#{Dir.home}/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db")')

  # Regression guard: no relative ../scripts sh call anywhere in the file.
  raise "FAIL: another relative ../scripts sh call exists in the Fastfile" \
    if source.match?(/^\s*sh\(.*"\.\.\/scripts\//)

  puts "gh-1910: build_only keychain helper resolved via __dir__ — all checks passed"
end

# desktop wasm load would fail as a missing asset, not a
          # #1224-class "no lazy loader" stub.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh "$ASSETS" \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

          rm -f fa-macos-*.dmg tmp-fa.dmg
          rm -rf dmg-staging

          echo "Packaging: $APP_PATH → $DMG_NAME (arch: $ARCH)"

          if [ "$SIGNED" = "true" ] && [ -n "$CERT_SHA1" ]; then
            echo "Signing .app bundle..."

            RESVG_BIN="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/resvg"
            if [ -f "$RESVG_BIN" ]; then
              echo "Stripping extended attributes from resvg..."
              xattr -cr "$RESVG_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
              echo "Signing resvg binary..."
              codesign --force --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$RESVG_BIN"
            fi

            find "$APP_PATH" -type f \( -perm +111 -o -name '*.dylib' \) | while read -r bin; do
              if codesign -dv "$bin" 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "$CERT_NAME"; then
                continue
              fi
              echo "Signing nested binary: $bin"
              codesign --force --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
            done

            if [ "$PROFILE_EMBEDDED" = "true" ] && [ -f "profile.provisionprofile" ]; then
              echo "Embedding provisioning profile..."
              cp profile.provisionprofile "$APP_PATH/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile"
              APP_ID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
              TEAM_ID="${APP_ID%%.*}"
              # Start from Release.entitlements (network client+server, file
              # bookmarks, calendar, contacts, health, homekit, audio input)
              # and inject the provisioning identity keys — do NOT collapse
              # to a sandbox-only dict: the app needs every entitlement the
              # sandbox declares, and dropping them breaks SSO callback
              # servers, file access, and OS-level permission flows in the
              # signed production build.
              cp flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements entitlements.plist
              # PlistBuddy handles dotted top-level key names (plutil
              # -insert/-replace treats dots as nested key separators).
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.application-identifier string $APP_ID" entitlements.plist
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.developer.team-identifier string $TEAM_ID" entitlements.plist
              # The profile may not grant every *capability* the app declares
              # (e.g. homekit needs a separate App ID capability in the
              # Developer Portal). TestFlight rejects capability entitlements
              # the profile doesn't include ('Invalid Code Signing
              # Entitlements', error 90285).
              #
              # Only com.apple.developer.* keys are profile-gated. The
              # com.apple.security.* sandbox entitlements (network, files,
              # personal-information) are NOT in the profile by design — any
              # sandboxed app may declare them — so they must survive.
              #
              # NOTE: `plutil -extract ... -o -` (stdout form) is not
              # supported on every macOS the runner may have; use real temp
              # files so the extraction can't silently produce nothing.
              security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile -o profile_decoded.plist
              plutil -extract Entitlements json profile_decoded.plist -o profile_ents.json
              for KEY in $(plutil -convert xml1 entitlements.plist -o - | grep -o '<key>[^<]*</key>' | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'); do
                case "$KEY" in
                  com.apple.application-identifier|com.apple.developer.team-identifier) continue ;;
                  com.apple.developer.*) ;;
                  *) continue ;; # sandbox + misc entitlements are not profile-gated
                esac
                if ! python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('profile_ents.json')); raise SystemExit(0 if '$KEY' in d else 1)"; then
                  echo "Dropping capability not granted by profile: $KEY"
                  /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Delete :$KEY" entitlements.plist
                fi
              done
              ENTITLEMENTS="entitlements.plist"
            else
              ENTITLEMENTS="flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements"
            fi

            codesign_app() {
              codesign --force --deep --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" \
                "$APP_PATH"
            }

            for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
              if codesign_app; then
                break
              fi

# 🚨 BLOCKING: committed private key (`privkey.pem`) — red CI + secret hygiene

Commit `e8ef159825` ("gh-1865 r2 reconciliation") adds `privkey.pem` (28 lines,
1.7 KB, `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` on line 1) at the **repo root**. Nothing
in the repo references it — `grep -rn privkey` over `*.dart|*.yml|*.yaml|*.sh`
returns zero hits, and the new behavioral fixture suite
(`test/ci_profile_serial_precheck_test.dart`) generates its **own** key into
`Directory.systemTemp` at runtime, so this file is not a test input. It looks
like a stray artifact of the fixture-keychain work that got committed with the
reconciliation commit.

This is not just hygiene — it is the **observed red CI** on the head
(`ci_failures.md`, Static gates, run 40721354969):

```
Package validation found the following error:
* line 1, column 1 of privkey.pem: Potential leak of Private Key detected.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 65.
```

The publish dry-run stages the repo-root payload (`scripts/stage_publish_package.sh`),
`.pubignore` excludes only sub-projects — so `privkey.pem` ships in the package
surface and the pub leak detector aborts. GitHub's log shows the content was
redacted as a live private-key pattern.

**Fix**

```bash
git rm privkey.pem
```

Optionally add `/privkey.pem` to `.gitignore` so a future fixture run at the
repo root cannot be committed again.

**If this is anything other than the disposable `openssl req` fixture key**
(i.e. it protects anything real), treat it as an actual leak: rotate the key
and consider history scrubbing — a force-push rebase is already part of this
PR's workflow.

# 🚨 BLOCKING: retired helper's Ruby guard test left behind — `flutter-tests` leg will go red

The PR deletes `scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh` and its **Dart** tests
(`ci_keychain_searchlist_add_behavior_test.dart`,
`ci_keychain_searchlist_union_guard_test.dart`) — but the **Ruby** guard from
gh-1910, `flutter_app/fastlane/test/build_only_keychain_helper_test.rb`, still
asserts the retired world and is run by CI:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2095-2102` ("Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)")
  iterates `for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do ruby "$t"; done` —
  the first non-zero exit kills the step (default `bash -e`).

Verified against this head:

```
$ ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/build_only_keychain_helper_test.rb
...: FAIL: build_only does not resolve the helper from the Fastfile location
     (File.expand_path("../../scripts/keychain_searchlist_add.sh", __dir__)) (RuntimeError)
```

It raises because the lane now contains `sh(ci_sign, "unlock")` (this line) and
the helper file no longer exists. The observed red run (Static gates) aborted
at the publish leak before `flutter-tests` reported — this is the **latent
second red**: the very next CI pass on a fixed head fails here.

**Why the PR's own guard missed it**: AC4's `_keychainSurfaces` in
`test/ci_sign_host_keychain_guard_test.dart` scans `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
the `Fastfile`, and `scripts/*.sh` — `flutter_app/fastlane/test/*.rb` is a
blind spot, so the "no surface may reference `keychain_searchlist_add`" audit
passed while a live reference remained.

**Fix**

1. Delete `flutter_app/fastlane/test/build_only_keychain_helper_test.rb`
   (its cwd-independence lesson is already carried by the Fastfile's
   `File.expand_path` comment), or rewrite it to pin the new contract
   (`sh(ci_sign, "unlock")` present and preceding `build_app(`).
2. Add `flutter_app/fastlane/test/*.rb` to `_keychainSurfaces` so AC4 can
   never miss a Ruby reference to a retired helper again.

# 🚨 BLOCKING: `security cms -D` remnants on the signed DMG path contradict model v3's own premise

This PR's rationale (stated in the PR's own changed lines) is that
`security cms -D` requires a default keychain and model v3 never sets one:

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml:593-594` — "Decoding goes through ci-sign
  plist — `security cms -D` needs a default keychain, which this model never
  sets."
- `scripts/ci-sign` (`plist` command) — "`security cms -D` requires a default
  keychain (none exists on this host by design — default-keychain writes are
  part of the old race)."

On **main**, the DMG packaging step worked only because the import step had
earlier run `security default-keychain -s build-<arch>.keychain` in the same
job. This PR retires that flip — but leaves the DMG step's two decode calls
untouched:

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml:773`:
  `APP_ID=$(security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | …)`
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml:801`:
  `security cms -D -i profile.provisionprofile -o profile_decoded.plist`

Both execute on the **signed** path (`SIGNED=true && PROFILE_EMBEDDED=true`),
i.e. every production DMG run, *after* the multi-minute archive. Under model v3
there is no default keychain in play, so per the premise above both calls fail
(they run inside `set -euo pipefail` / `bash -e`) and the leg dies mid-packaging
— an expensive, avoidable red on the very class of host-state nondeterminism
this PR exists to eliminate. (If the premise is wrong and `cms -D` works
against the host's login keychain, then the plist/doctor migration rationale
itself needs revisiting — either way the inconsistency must be reconciled.)

**Fix** — route both through the same path as the migrated steps above:

```bash
APP_ID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile \
  | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - \
  | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 \
  | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
…
~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile -o profile_decoded.plist  # add -out plumbing or:
~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile > profile_decoded.plist
```

(`plist` writes the decoded payload to stdout, so `> file` replaces `-o file`
directly. Consider a guard-test assert that no `security cms` executable line
remains in workflow-land, mirroring AC1's keychain-write audit.)

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: confirm `security set-keychain-settings -u` (no `-t`) really means "no auto-lock"

`ensure_keychain` (this line) comments: "No inactivity auto-lock; explicit
unlock per operation keeps it honest." — but it only passes `-u`, no `-t`.
The semantics of `security set-keychain-settings` are notoriously easy to get
wrong here: the classic CI recipes always pair the flags (`-lut 720`), and the
documented default auto-lock timeout for a keychain is **300 seconds**. If the
unspecified `-t` leaves (or resets) the default window on the persistent
keychain, the gh-1798 failure class quietly returns with a 5-minute window:

- `ci-sign install` unlocks at provisioning time;
- the build-macos legs then run the full flutter build (~30–90 min) and sign
  in the DMG step with plain `codesign --sign "$CERT_SHA1"` — there is **no
  point-of-use unlock anywhere in build-macos.yml** (only the iOS Fastfile
  lane unlocks via `ci-sign unlock`);
- a locked non-interactive keychain surfaces as
  `errSecInteractionNotAllowed` / "User interaction is not allowed" mid-leg —
  exactly the retired `ci_macos_signing_window_guard_test.dart` scenario.

The guard test cannot catch this: AC1 only asserts that
`set-keychain-settings` is absent from workflow-land; the call now lives
inside `scripts/ci-sign`.

**Please confirm on the host** (one command):

```bash
security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db
```

- `…timeout=sec(0)` / no lock-interval → the model holds; nothing to do.
- `…timeout=300 sec(300)` (or any finite value) → add an explicit
  `security set-keychain-settings -u -t 999999 "$KC"` (or `-t` large) in
  `ensure_keychain`, and/or a `~/bin/ci-sign unlock` immediately before the
  DMG step's first `codesign` — mirroring the Fastfile's point-of-use unlock.

The e2e smoke in the test plan ran codesign right after install, so a
sub-5-minute gap would not have exposed this; the pending daily-publish
(parallel legs) is the first real probe.

# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: `~/bin/ci-sign` (host copy) vs `scripts/ci-sign` (checkout copy) — two sources of truth, no self-provisioning

Signing state now depends on an out-of-band host artifact, but the two call
sites disagree about which copy is authoritative:

- workflows (this line, build-macos.yml, host-signing-provision.yml) call the
  **host copy** `~/bin/ci-sign`;
- `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile:453-454` calls the **checkout copy**
  `File.expand_path("../../scripts/ci-sign", __dir__)`.

`host-signing-provision.yml` syncs repo → host, but only when dispatched. Two
concrete failure shapes:

1. **Fresh or wiped host / new registration** — a signing leg fails with
   `~/bin/ci-sign: command not found` mid-pipeline instead of provisioning
   itself; nothing in the workflow falls back to the checkout copy it already
   has.
2. **Silent skew** — a future PR changes `scripts/ci-sign` (say a new env
   contract) and merges without re-dispatching the provision workflow. The
   provision step then runs the OLD host copy while the Fastfile later runs
   the NEW checkout copy *in the same job* (e.g. host copy predates a changed
   `unlock` behavior) — an opaque mid-archive divergence.

**Suggested fix** (one line per signing job, removes the skew class without
changing the design): sync at job start from the checkout the job already has

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/bin" && cp scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign" && chmod +x "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
```

— or invoke `"$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/ci-sign"` everywhere and keep
`~/bin/ci-sign` as provision-only host tooling. The idempotent-install model
is explicitly safe for concurrent legs (lock-dir serialization), so doing the
copy in every signing job costs nothing and deletes the "forgot to
re-dispatch provision" foot-gun. A guard assert (all `ci-sign` invocations in
workflows resolve to the checkout copy) would pin it.

# 💡 SUGGESTION: `ci-sign install` — the highest-risk surface — has no behavioral test

`ci_profile_serial_precheck_test.dart` sets a great precedent: it runs the
**real** `scripts/ci-sign doctor` against a sandbox keychain
(`CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN` + fixture p12) covering every plist encoding plus both
failure teeth. `install` — the command that mutates persistent host state
(create/import/rotation/partition-list/manifest write) — only gets static
string asserts here (AC2). A same-shaped behavioral suite would pin the
teeth that actually caused the incident chain:

1. **idempotency**: two `install <label>` runs with the same fixture p12 →
   second is a no-op (`identity … is up to date`), manifest unchanged;
2. **rotation**: install p12-A, then p12-B for the same label → A's identity
   is gone from the keychain (delete-identity path), manifest carries B's
   sha1;
3. **invalid p12 / wrong password** → exit 1 with the "cannot read P12" error,
   manifest not written, keychain untouched;
4. **verify teeth**: corrupt the manifest's `sha1=` line → `ci-sign sha1
   <label>` dies with "corrupt manifest" instead of silently falling through
   to a same-named identity (the AC4 invariant, exercised for real);
5. **lock contention** (optional): hold `$CFG/install.lock` → install waits,
   then dies with "holds the lock" after the 120 s budget.

All of it already works on the `CI_SIGN_KEYCHAIN` override the doctor tests
use — no macOS-host assumptions beyond what the precheck suite already makes.

# 💡 SUGGESTION: validate the label argument before using it in file paths

`install <label>` (this line) flows straight into manifest paths:
`$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL` for both read (`sed -n 's/^sha1=//p' "$LABELS_DIR/$LABEL"`)
and write. A label like `../foo` or `a/b` escapes the labels directory. The
callers are trusted workflows passing three fixed literals (`ios`, `macos`,
`macos-installer`), so this is defense-in-depth, not an exploitable surface —
but the script is also documented as a general host tool (`ci-sign list`,
manual smoke), and a one-line allowlist keeps the manifest directory honest:

```bash
case "$LABEL" in
  [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*) ;;                       # labels are short dns-ish slugs
  *) die "invalid label '$LABEL' (expected [a-z0-9-])" ;;
esac
```

The same guard naturally covers the `sha1|serial|name` and `codesign` branches
(they read the same manifest path at lines 250/260).

Review complete. **PR #1944 (gh-1865 signing model v3)** verdict: **REQUEST_CHANGES** — the ci-sign design is sound (persistent host keychain, SHA-1 identity pinning, fail-fast `doctor`, parallel matrix restored), but the head is red and two latent correctness gaps must be fixed:

1. 🚨 **`privkey.pem` committed at repo root** — an unreferenced PEM private-key artifact from the fixture work; it's the exact cause of the observed red Static gates (pub leak detector, exit 65). `git rm` required; escalate to rotation if it's not the disposable openssl fixture key.
2. 🚨 **Stale Ruby guard** — `flutter_app/fastlane/test/build_only_keychain_helper_test.rb` still asserts the deleted `keychain_searchlist_add.sh` (verified failing locally); CI runs every `fastlane/test/*_test.rb`, so the flutter-tests leg is a guaranteed second red. The AC4 guard's surface list misses `fastlane/test/*.rb` — that blind spot let it through.
3. 🚨 **`security cms -D` remnants** at build-macos.yml:773/801 on the signed DMG path — contradicts the PR's own premise ("cms -D needs a default keychain, which this model never sets") now that the `default-keychain` flip is retired; route through `~/bin/ci-sign plist` like the migrated steps.
4. ⚠️ Confirm `set-keychain-settings -u` without `-t` really means no auto-lock (if a 300 s default applies, the DMG leg re-creates gh-1798 mid-build); ⚠️ `~/bin/ci-sign` host copy vs checkout copy drift, no fallback/self-provisioning. Plus 3 suggestions (dead `want` var, no behavioral tests for `install`, label path validation).

Note: some `[REDACTED:…]` tokens seen while reading files were output-pipeline artifacts (verified against raw bytes — the real file content is intact); `dart analyze`/`dart test` could not run in this sandbox (no package config, offline resolve fails), so guard-test assertions were verified by direct inspection and the Ruby guard by execution.
